Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 95, verse 1:

﴿Wa-t-tīni wa-z-zaytūn﴾ — i.e., the two edible fruits; or two mountains in al-Sham (Greater Syria) which produce the two edible fruits.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 95, verse 2:

﴿And Mount Sinai﴾ The mountain upon which Allah the Exalted spoke to Musa (Moses). The meaning of Sinin is "the blessed" or "the beautiful, abounding in fruit-bearing trees."
ِ﴿And this secure land﴾ — Makkah, for people are safe in it, in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance) and in Islam.
"﴿We have certainly created man﴾ the species, ﴿in the best of stature﴾ meaning, the proportioning of his form."

﴿Then We returned him﴾ in some of his kind, ﴿to the lowest of the low﴾, a kināya (an indirect, figurative expression) for decrepitude and weakness. So the deed of the believer decreases compared with the time of youth, and he will still have his reward.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on verse 95:6

﴿Illa﴾ (but, "except") meaning: rather, ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them there is a reward never cut off﴾ meaning: uninterrupted. And in a hadith: "When the believer reaches such an old age that it prevents him from doing deeds, there is written for him what he used to do."

﴿So what causes you to deny﴾ O disbeliever ﴿after﴾ what has been mentioned of the creation of man in the best form, and then His returning him to the lowest state of old age, which shows the power to resurrect, ﴿the Judgment﴾, meaning the recompense that follows resurrection and reckoning. That is, what makes you a denier of it, when there is none who causes it to be?

Qur'an 95:8: "Is not Allah the most just of judges?"

Al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) say: He is the most decisive of judges (aqda al-qadin), and His judgment concerning the recompense is part of that. And in the hadith: "Whoever recites 'By the fig' (al-Tin) through to its end, let him say: 'Yes, and I am among those who bear witness to that.'"
